failure_reason: The decomposition captures the intended creative-microscoping proof and all nine lemmas are individually plausible; L3 and especially L5 are the explicit bottlenecks. The main issues are formal rather than mathematical: step A7 is mislabeled as trivial, and step A9 applies the Laurent-polynomial cancellation lemma L9 to H=T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q) without showing H is Laurent (the displayed theorem sum is generally a rational function with denominator built from U_{d,n}). The final cancellation therefore needs a localization/rational-function version of L9 or an explicit ambient-ring definition for the congruence.

strategy_summary: Introduce an auxiliary parameter a by replacing the repeated factor (q^r,q^r;q^{2d})_k with (a q^r, q^r/a;q^{2d})_k. Rewrite the original summand so that its only denominator is (-q^d;q^d)_k, then clear that harmless denominator by U_{d,n}(q)=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}). This yields a polynomial P_{d,r,n}(a,q) in a with Laurent-polynomial coefficients in q. Prove that P_{d,r,n}(a,q) vanishes at a=q^{rn} and a=q^{-rn} (special-value exact evaluations) and also at every nontrivial nth root of unity in the q-variable (root-of-unity vanishing). These give divisibility by (1-aq^{rn})(a-q^{rn}) and by [n]_q, respectively. Because the two factors are coprime, P_{d,r,n}(a,q) is divisible by their product. Specialize a=1; then (1-q^{rn})^2 contributes Φ_n(q)^2, and cancelling U_{d,n}(q) recovers the stated congruence modulo [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.
